### 1. Incorporate "Tempo" Runs
Instead of just running at a steady, comfortable pace, try a tempo run once a week. This involves running at a pace that feels "comfortably hard" (around your goal 5K race pace or slightly slower) for 20–30 minutes. This helps improve your lactate threshold, which is the point at which your body starts to fatigue quickly.

### 2. Add Interval Training
Intervals are excellent for speed and VO2 max improvement. Find a track or a flat stretch of road and try this:
*   **Warm-up:** 10 minutes of easy jogging.
*   **The Workout:** Run 800 meters (or 3-4 minutes) at a speed faster than your goal race pace, followed by a 2-minute recovery jog. Repeat this 4–5 times.
*   **Cool-down:** 10 minutes of easy jogging.

### 3. The Weekly "Long Run"
Even though a 5K is a short distance, increasing your weekly long run is one of the best ways to build aerobic endurance. Aim to make one run per week longer than your usual training runs—gradually build this up to 7 or 8 kilometers. The extra time on your feet will make your usual 5K run feel much shorter and easier on race day.
